comments.note: LabelCleanerViewModel: backing field _uCWords (non-standard casing) is needed to make CommunityToolkit.Mvvm's source generator produce the property name UCWords (the generator capitalises only the first character after stripping the underscore prefix). This is a known limitation of the generator's naming convention when the desired property name starts with multiple uppercase letters. A code comment in the file would make this clear for future maintainers.

MovieEditorViewModel.CleanLabelCommand always constructs LabelCleanerOptions with defaults (new LabelCleanerOptions()) rather than reading the current AppOptions.LabelCleaner. This is intentional for MVP simplicity — the user can toggle options in the dialog. If persisted option state is desired in a future iteration, inject ISettingsService and read settings.Current.LabelCleaner as the initial options.

FakeMovieRepository.GetOriginalFilenameAsync always returns null (no SetOriginalFilename helper). The CleanLabelCommand test therefore exercises the fallback path (rawInput = LabelText). A future test for the primary path (when originalFilename is non-null) would require extending FakeMovieRepository with a SetOriginalFilename configuration method.

comments.note: Added explanatory comment above _uCWords backing field in LabelCleanerViewModel.cs. The field uses non-standard lowercase-u casing (_uCWords rather than _UCWords) because CommunityToolkit.Mvvm's source generator strips the leading underscore and capitalises only the first remaining character — so _uCWords produces the intended property name UCWords. The comment prevents future maintainers from 'correcting' the casing and breaking the generated property name.

AvaloniaLabelCleanerService correctly unsubscribes the EventHandler<LabelCleanerResult?> in a try/finally block — no memory leak risk. Pattern is consistent with AvaloniaConnectionEditorService and AvaloniaMoviePropertiesService.

LabelCleanerViewModel initialises its backing fields directly in the full constructor (_preserveDates, _uCWords, _stripKeywords) rather than using the generated setters. This prevents three spurious RunParse() calls during construction — the initial parse is then fired once explicitly at the end of the constructor. Good pattern, consistent with MovieEditorViewModel's construction discipline.

FakeNameParser and FakeLabelCleanerService expose call-count tracking (ParseCallCount, ShowCallCount) and last-argument capture (LastOptions, LastViewModel). This is a reusable pattern worth applying to future test helper fakes in the same project.

[documentation-forward] api-surface.md entry for LabelCleanerViewModel should document the _uCWords / UCWords generator naming constraint in the property listing so future readers understand why the property is named UCWords but the Observable field uses non-PascalCase casing.
